para: The subclassical graph serves as a benchmark for the expressiveness and computational power of logical calculi in a sense that no pairwise comparison can provide: a calculus's position in the graph — its extensions, its embeddings, the cardinality and composition of its duality orbit — gives a structural fingerprint that can be compared across the entire landscape at once. This fingerprint is the natural unit for the decision problem that was Tarski's starting point and that remains the organizing problem of the present work: the question of decidability, semi-decidability, and essential undecidability for theories formulated in non-classical logical frameworks does not have the same answer in every region of the graph, and the graph is the tool that makes it possible to ask the question with the precision it requires. An automated reasoning system modeled on the graph — one that represents its inference engine as a navigable subgraph and selects proof strategies by traversing duality and extension edges — is a natural engineering consequence of the theoretical framework, and its development constitutes one of the later aims of this project.
